sections.content:
THIS DEED OF PARTNERSHIP is made at Kolkata, West Bengal on [DATE] BETWEEN (1) Mr. Aarav Mehta, aged [AGE] years, son of [FATHER'S NAME OF AARAV MEHTA], residing at [ADDRESS OF AARAV MEHTA] (hereinafter referred to as "the First Partner", which expression shall, unless repugnant to the context, include his heirs, executors, administrators and legal representatives), of the First Part; (2) Mr. Rohan Sen, aged [AGE] years, son of [FATHER'S NAME OF ROHAN SEN], residing at [ADDRESS OF ROHAN SEN] (hereinafter referred to as "the Second Partner", which expression shall, unless repugnant to the context, include his heirs, executors, administrators and legal representatives), of the Second Part; and (3) Ms. Priya Kapoor, aged [AGE] years, daughter of [FATHER'S NAME OF PRIYA KAPOOR], residing at [ADDRESS OF PRIYA KAPOOR] (hereinafter referred to as "the Third Partner", which expression shall, unless repugnant to the context, include her heirs, executors, administrators and legal representatives), of the Third Part. The First Partner, the Second Partner and the Third Partner are hereinafter collectively referred to as "the Partners" and individually as "a Partner", which expressions shall, unless repugnant to the context, include their respective heirs, executors, administrators and legal representatives.

WHEREAS the Partners have agreed to associate themselves as partners for carrying on the business of business consultancy and corporate compliance services under the firm name of Mehta Sen & Associates upon the terms and conditions hereinafter contained.

AND WHEREAS the Partners are desirous of reducing the terms of their partnership into writing.

NOW THIS DEED WITNESSETH AS FOLLOWS:

1. That the business of the partnership shall be carried on under the firm name and style of "Mehta Sen & Associates" (hereinafter referred to as "the Firm").

2. That the business of the Firm shall be that of business consultancy and corporate compliance services, including advisory, secretarial, regulatory compliance and allied professional services, and such other lawful business as the Partners may from time to time unanimously agree in writing to add, change or discontinue.

3. That the principal place of business of the Firm shall be at [PRINCIPAL OFFICE ADDRESS, KOLKATA, WEST BENGAL], and the Firm may open branch offices at such other places as the Partners may unanimously decide in writing.

4. That the partnership shall be deemed to have commenced business with effect from [COMMENCEMENT DATE].

5. That the partnership hereby constituted is a partnership at will within the meaning of section 7 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (exact section to be confirmed), and shall continue until dissolved in accordance with this Deed or by operation of law. [IF A FIXED TERM IS INTENDED, INSTRUCTING ADVOCATE TO CONFIRM AND SUBSTITUTE THIS CLAUSE ACCORDINGLY.]

6. That the Firm is presently unregistered. The Partners note that under section 69 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, an unregistered firm is barred from instituting a suit to enforce a right arising from a contract against a third party or against a co-partner, and the Partners record their intention to apply for registration of the Firm with the Registrar of Firms, West Bengal, under section 58 of the Act at the earliest, and in any event before the Firm has occasion to enforce any such right by suit.

7. That the total capital of the Firm shall be Rs. 20,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakh only), contributed by the Partners as follows: (a) Mr. Aarav Mehta shall contribute Rs. 10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakh only); (b) Mr. Rohan Sen shall contribute Rs. 6,00,000/- (Rupees Six Lakh only); and (c) Ms. Priya Kapoor shall contribute Rs. 4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakh only), the whole of such capital having been brought in and credited to the respective capital accounts of the Partners in the books of the Firm as on the date of commencement.

8. That interest on capital shall be payable to each Partner at the rate of 12% (twelve percent) per annum, or at such other rate as may from time to time be prescribed as the maximum allowable deduction under section 40(b) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, whichever is lower, and such interest shall be credited to the respective capital or current accounts of the Partners at the close of each financial year, subject to the Firm having profits from which such interest may be paid.

9. That no Partner shall be entitled to withdraw any part of the capital standing to the credit of that Partner's capital account except with the prior written consent of all the Partners, or as expressly permitted under this Deed on retirement, death or dissolution.

10. That the net profits of the Firm, after payment of interest on capital, remuneration to working Partners, and all outgoings and expenses of the business, shall be divided among the Partners, and all losses (including losses of capital) shall be borne by the Partners, in the ratio of 50:30:20 (fifty is to thirty is to twenty), that is to say: (a) Mr. Aarav Mehta - 50% (fifty percent); (b) Mr. Rohan Sen - 30% (thirty percent); and (c) Ms. Priya Kapoor - 20% (twenty percent).

11. That the above ratio shall apply to both profits and losses of the Firm unless varied by a supplementary deed executed by all the Partners in writing.

12. That each Partner may draw, on account of that Partner's anticipated share of profits, such sums by way of monthly or periodic drawings as the Partners may unanimously fix in writing from time to time, provided that such drawings shall not exceed the drawing Partner's estimated share of profits for that financial year and shall be adjusted against the final division of profits.

13. That such of the Partners as are working partners of the Firm, being [NAMES OF WORKING PARTNERS - ASSUMED TO BE ALL THREE PARTNERS UNLESS OTHERWISE INSTRUCTED], shall be entitled to remuneration (salary) for the conduct of the business of the Firm, such remuneration to be computed and allowed in aggregate only within the limits prescribed under section 40(b) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, and to be apportioned among the working Partners in the ratio of [REMUNERATION APPORTIONMENT RATIO - TO BE CONFIRMED] or in such other manner as the Partners may unanimously agree in writing, subject always to the statutory ceiling.

14. That interest on any credit balance in a Partner's current account, and on any debit balance in a Partner's current account payable by that Partner to the Firm, shall be charged or allowed, as the case may be, at the rate of 12% (twelve percent) per annum or at the maximum rate permissible for deduction under section 40(b) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, whichever is lower.

15. That the remuneration and interest referred to in this Section shall be subject to, and shall not exceed, the limits from time to time prescribed under section 40(b) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, so that the same remains an allowable deduction in computing the taxable income of the Firm.

16. That the business of the Firm shall be managed jointly by all the Partners, each of whom shall be entitled to take part in the conduct of the business under section 12(a) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.

17. That notwithstanding clause 16, the following acts shall require the prior written consent of all the Partners: (a) borrowing or lending money in excess of Rs. [THRESHOLD AMOUNT] on behalf of the Firm; (b) purchase, sale, mortgage or charge of any immovable property of the Firm; (c) admission of a new partner or introduction of a partner under section 31; (d) any compromise, settlement, submission to arbitration, or reference of a dispute concerning the Firm's business exceeding Rs. [THRESHOLD AMOUNT] in value; (e) opening or closing of any bank account of the Firm; (f) any act that would bind the Firm as surety or guarantor for a third party; and (g) any change in the nature of the business of the Firm.

18. That every Partner shall, in accordance with section 9 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, carry on the business of the Firm to the greatest common advantage, be just and faithful to the other Partners, and render true accounts and full information of all things affecting the Firm to any Partner or his or her legal representative.

19. That every Partner shall, in accordance with section 10 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, indemnify the Firm for any loss caused to it by that Partner's fraud in the conduct of the business of the Firm.

20. That no Partner shall, without the consent of the other Partners, engage in any other business or profession for gain while remaining a Partner of the Firm, save such existing engagements as have been disclosed in writing prior to the execution of this Deed, if any.

sections.section_name: BANK ACCOUNTS AND BOOKS OF ACCOUNT
sections.content:
21. That the Firm shall maintain one or more bank accounts in its name with such bank or banks as the Partners may unanimously decide, and such accounts shall be operated jointly by [NAMES OF AUTHORISED SIGNATORIES], or singly by any one Partner up to a limit of Rs. [DAILY/TRANSACTION LIMIT], beyond which the joint signature of at least two Partners shall be required, as the Partners may unanimously resolve in writing from time to time.

22. That proper books of account of the Firm shall be maintained at the principal place of business of the Firm referred to in clause 3 above, on a mercantile or such other basis as is consistently applied, and shall be closed and balanced at the end of each financial year ending on the 31st of March.

23. That every Partner shall, in accordance with section 12(d) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, have the right to have access to, and to inspect and take copies of, the books of account of the Firm at all reasonable times.

24. That no person shall be introduced as a partner of the Firm without the consent of all the existing Partners, in accordance with section 31 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, and any such admission shall be recorded in a supplementary deed executed by all Partners (including the incoming partner), specifying the incoming partner's capital contribution and revised profit-sharing ratio.

25. That any Partner may retire from the Firm by giving not less than 3 (three) months' prior written notice to the other Partners, in accordance with section 32 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. The retiring Partner shall remain liable for all acts of the Firm done before retirement, and shall continue to be liable to third parties for acts of the Firm done after retirement until public notice of retirement is given as contemplated under section 32.

26. That a Partner may be expelled from the Firm by a resolution passed by not less than [PROPORTION, E.G. THREE-FOURTHS] in value of the shares of the remaining Partners, exercised in good faith, and only for grave cause such as persistent breach of this Deed, conduct prejudicial to the business of the Firm, or gross misconduct, in accordance with section 33 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. No expulsion shall take effect unless the Partner sought to be expelled has been given a written notice setting out the grounds and a reasonable opportunity to be heard.

27. That the capital, current account balance and share in the assets of a retiring or expelled Partner shall be determined and paid out in the manner set out in clause 29 below.

sections.section_name: DEATH AND INSOLVENCY OF A PARTNER
sections.content:
28. That the Firm shall not stand dissolved by reason of the death of a Partner, and the surviving Partners shall have the option, exercisable within 3 (three) months of the death, either to continue the business of the Firm with the legal heirs or legal representatives of the deceased Partner (if such legal heirs or legal representatives are willing and are admitted by unanimous written consent of the surviving Partners), or to continue the business among themselves alone, paying out the estate of the deceased Partner in accordance with clause 29 below. This clause is intended to displace, as between the Partners, the default rule of dissolution on death that would otherwise apply, to the extent permitted by section 42(c) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (exact scope to be confirmed).

29. That upon the death, retirement, expulsion or insolvency of a Partner, the value of the outgoing or deceased Partner's share shall be ascertained by preparing accounts of the Firm as on the date of such event (including a valuation of goodwill, if any, on a basis to be unanimously agreed or, failing agreement, determined by a Chartered Accountant appointed by the continuing Partners), and the amount found due, comprising the balance in the capital and current accounts together with the proportionate share in the profits and losses of the Firm up to that date computed in the ratio at clause 10, shall be paid to the outgoing Partner, or to the legal heirs or legal representatives of the deceased Partner, in [NUMBER] equal instalments over a period of [PERIOD, E.G. 12 (TWELVE) MONTHS] from the date of ascertainment, together with interest at the rate of [RATE]% per annum on the outstanding balance, or on such other terms as may be unanimously agreed in writing.

30. That in the event any Partner is adjudicated insolvent, such Partner shall cease to be a partner of the Firm with effect from the date of the order of adjudication, in accordance with section 34 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, and the Firm shall, at the option of the remaining Partners, either stand dissolved as to such Partner or continue between the remaining Partners, the insolvent Partner's share being ascertained and paid to the Official Assignee or Official Receiver, as the case may be, in the manner set out in clause 29 above.

31. That no Partner shall sell, transfer, assign, mortgage or otherwise encumber that Partner's share or interest in the Firm, or any part thereof, without the prior written consent of all the other Partners.

32. That any transfer made in contravention of clause 31, or any transfer made with consent, shall, in accordance with section 29 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, entitle the transferee only to receive the share of profits of the transferring Partner and to be bound by the accounts of the Firm as agreed to by the other Partners, and shall not, during the continuance of the Firm, entitle the transferee to interfere in the conduct of the business, to require accounts, or to inspect the books of the Firm; and upon dissolution the transferee shall be entitled only to the transferring Partner's share of the assets as valued by agreement among the Partners or, failing agreement, by an accounting from the date of dissolution.

33. That each Partner shall keep confidential, both during the continuance of the partnership and thereafter, all client information, business methods, financial data and proprietary information of the Firm, and shall not disclose the same to any third party except as required in the ordinary course of the Firm's business or by law.

34. That during the continuance of the partnership, no Partner shall, without the consent of the other Partners, carry on any business competing with the business of the Firm, in accordance with section 11(2) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.

35. That a restraint on a Partner carrying on a similar business after ceasing to be a partner is valid only within the narrow limits permitted under section 36(2) (restraint on a former partner within specified local limits, for a reasonable period, upon sale of goodwill or otherwise) and section 54 (restraint pending settlement of accounts after dissolution) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, read with section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which renders void any agreement in restraint of trade save to the extent expressly saved by these provisions. Accordingly, the Partners agree that any outgoing Partner shall not, for a period of [PERIOD, NOT EXCEEDING WHAT IS REASONABLE] from the date of ceasing to be a partner, and within [SPECIFIED LOCAL LIMITS, E.G. THE LIMITS OF THE KOLKATA MUNICIPAL CORPORATION], solicit clients of the Firm with whom that Partner had direct dealing while a partner; this restraint is drawn narrowly to fall within section 36(2) and section 54, and the Partners record that any wider restraint on an outgoing Partner's freedom to carry on a competing business would be void under section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and is not intended by this Deed.

36. That, as between the Partners themselves, each Partner shall indemnify and keep indemnified the other Partners against any loss caused to the Firm by that Partner's wilful neglect, fraud, or conduct in excess of the authority conferred by this Deed, in the manner contemplated under section 10 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.

37. That the Partners expressly record, in accordance with sections 18 to 27 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, that every Partner is an agent of the Firm and of the other Partners for the purposes of the business of the Firm, and every Partner shall be liable, jointly and severally with the other Partners, to third parties for all acts of the Firm done while that Partner was a partner. The indemnity in clause 36 operates only as between the Partners inter se to allocate the ultimate burden of loss, and does not and cannot limit, exclude or affect the joint and several liability of any Partner to a third party.

38. That any dispute, difference or claim arising out of or in connection with this Deed, or the construction, validity, interpretation, or breach thereof, or touching the affairs of the Firm, shall be referred to arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

39. That the arbitration shall be conducted by a sole arbitrator to be appointed by mutual consent of the Partners, or, failing such consent within 30 (thirty) days of a notice invoking arbitration, in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

40. That the seat and venue of arbitration shall be Kolkata, West Bengal, and the language of the arbitration proceedings shall be English. The award of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on the Partners, subject to the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

41. That the Firm may be dissolved: (a) by mutual consent of all the Partners; (b) on the happening of any event that makes it unlawful for the business of the Firm to be carried on; (c) by notice in writing by any Partner where the partnership is at will, as contemplated under this Deed; or (d) by order of a competent court, in accordance with the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.

42. That upon dissolution of the Firm, the accounts of the Firm shall be settled in the order prescribed under section 48 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, namely: firstly, in paying the debts of the Firm to third parties; secondly, in paying to each Partner rateably what is due to that Partner from the Firm for advances as distinguished from capital; thirdly, in paying to each Partner rateably what is due to that Partner on account of capital; and the residue, if any, shall be divided among the Partners in the profit-sharing ratio set out in clause 10 of this Deed, that is, 50:30:20 (fifty is to thirty is to twenty) as between Mr. Aarav Mehta, Mr. Rohan Sen and Ms. Priya Kapoor respectively.

43. That if the assets are insufficient to meet the debts and advances referred to above, the deficiency shall be borne by the Partners in the same ratio in which they share losses under clause 10.

44. That the Firm's books of account, records and the firm name shall, upon dissolution, be dealt with as the Partners may unanimously agree, and in the absence of agreement, as directed by the arbitrator under clause 38.

45. That no amendment, variation or modification of this Deed shall be valid unless made in writing and signed by all the Partners.

46. That any notice required to be given under this Deed shall be in writing and shall be deemed to be duly served if delivered by hand, sent by registered post with acknowledgment due, or by email with delivery confirmation, to the address of the Partner last known to the Firm, being for the present: Mr. Aarav Mehta at [ADDRESS OF AARAV MEHTA]; Mr. Rohan Sen at [ADDRESS OF ROHAN SEN]; and Ms. Priya Kapoor at [ADDRESS OF PRIYA KAPOOR].

47. That this Deed shall be governed by the laws of India, and, subject to clause 38 to 40 above, the courts at Kolkata, West Bengal shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any matter not referable to, or arising in the course of, arbitration, including applications under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF the Partners have set their respective hands on the date first above written.

SIGNED AND DELIVERED by Mr. Aarav Mehta (First Partner) __________________________ Name: Aarav Mehta Address: [ADDRESS OF AARAV MEHTA]

SIGNED AND DELIVERED by Mr. Rohan Sen (Second Partner) __________________________ Name: Rohan Sen Address: [ADDRESS OF ROHAN SEN]

SIGNED AND DELIVERED by Ms. Priya Kapoor (Third Partner) __________________________ Name: Priya Kapoor Address: [ADDRESS OF PRIYA KAPOOR]

WITNESSES:

1. Signature: __________________________ Name: [WITNESS 1 NAME] Address: [WITNESS 1 ADDRESS]

2. Signature: __________________________ Name: [WITNESS 2 NAME] Address: [WITNESS 2 ADDRESS]

assumptions.assumption: The ages, parentage and full residential addresses of Aarav Mehta, Rohan Sen and Priya Kapoor were not supplied and have been left as placeholders.
assumptions.why: These particulars are mandatory recitals in the PARTIES AND DATE section and cannot be invented.

assumptions.assumption: The exact principal office address in Kolkata and the commencement date of the partnership were not supplied.
assumptions.why: Required by the FIRM NAME, BUSINESS AND OFFICE section; only the city and state (Kolkata, West Bengal) were given.

assumptions.assumption: The partnership has been drafted as a partnership at will, since no fixed term was instructed.
assumptions.why: The Act defaults to partnership at will absent a fixed term; this is flagged in the document for confirmation and easy substitution if a fixed term is intended.

assumptions.assumption: All three partners have been treated as working partners entitled to remuneration under section 40(b) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, in the absence of any instruction distinguishing active from sleeping partners.
assumptions.why: Remuneration clauses require identification of working partners; no such distinction was given in the instructions.

assumptions.assumption: Interest on capital and on current accounts has been fixed at 12% per annum (subject to the section 40(b) ceiling), and the remuneration apportionment ratio, transaction thresholds for joint bank signature, expulsion voting threshold, and death/insolvency payout period and instalments have been left as placeholders or indicative figures for the instructing advocate to fix.
assumptions.why: No numeric instructions were given for these mechanical terms.

assumptions.assumption: The Firm is currently unregistered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
assumptions.why: No registration number or Registrar of Firms details were supplied; this has been noted as a fact to be confirmed rather than assumed registered.

drafting_notes.issue: The profit and loss sharing ratio of 50:30:20 as between Aarav Mehta, Rohan Sen and Priya Kapoor respectively has been reproduced exactly as instructed in clause 10 and applied consistently to the residue on dissolution under clause 42, and to the bearing of losses/deficiency under clause 43.
drafting_notes.recommendation: No action needed; confirm the ratio is correctly matched to the named partners in the order intended by the client before execution.

drafting_notes.issue: The non-compete clause (clause 35) restraining an outgoing partner from soliciting clients post-exit is drafted narrowly to fit within sections 36(2) and 54 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 read with section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, but the period and local limits are left as placeholders.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Instructing advocate must fix a reasonable time period and specific local limits before execution; an unreasonably wide or open-ended restraint risks being struck down as void under section 27 of the Contract Act.

drafting_notes.issue: The exact section reference for 'partnership at will' (used as section 7 in clause 5) and for the displacement of default dissolution-on-death rule (used as section 42(c) in clause 28) have been included but marked 'exact section to be confirmed' / 'exact scope to be confirmed' since they were not independently verified against the statute text in this context.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Verify sections 7 and 42(c) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (or the correct corresponding provisions) against the bare Act before filing or execution, and remove the confirmation flags once verified.

drafting_notes.issue: The Firm is unregistered as of drafting. Under section 69 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, this bars the Firm (and, in respect of a right vested in the Firm, its partners) from suing to enforce a contractual right against third parties or between partners, until registered.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Advise the client to apply for registration under section 58 promptly; do not rely on this Deed alone to enforce rights by suit until registration is completed.

drafting_notes.issue: Liability to third parties has been correctly stated as joint and several under sections 18 to 27, and the internal indemnity in clause 36 is expressly limited to allocation of burden inter se, consistent with the rule that liability to third parties cannot be contractually limited.
drafting_notes.recommendation: No further action needed; ensure this distinction is preserved in any future amendment.
